criteria.name: Findable
criteria.practice: Deposit datasets in a searchable FAIR-compliant data repository.
questions: Does the dataset have a resolvable PID: ARK, CSTR, DOI, IGSN, PURL, URN, HDL?
Does the dataset have a compact ID whose prefix is registered with identifiers.org (e.g., ena.embl:ERP001234, geo:GSE68086, dbgap:phs000001)?
Is the dataset deposited in a repository listed in re3data or FAIRsharing?

scoring.2: PID or prefix-registered compact ID is present, and the dataset was deposited in a registered repository.
scoring.1: Re3data or FAIRsharing registry is provided without a PID; or only a PID is given, but the dataset is not in a registered repository.
scoring.0: Neither is present.

criteria.name: Transparent
criteria.practice: Identify data sources traceable to a reasonable ground truth, e.g., clinical data from EHR at a given hospital, clinical trials, or laboratory data.
questions: Does the metadata identify the data's source specifically enough to reach a real-world, trustworthy ground truth? E.g., a named EHR/hospital, a named drug trial, a named lab; for experimental labs, the ground truth must include samples, instruments, reagents, and generated dataset.
Is the source metadata provided in machine-readable form? Valid ontologies are: W3C PROV-O, PROV-DM, or a derivation of either, e.g., EVI, CPM, PAV.

scoring.2: A source is named and traceable to a ground truth, in a structured metadata field.
scoring.1: The source is stated but not to a fully grounded truth, e.g., to a hospital but not to an actual OMOP dataset, or to an experimental lab dataset but not specifying samples, reagents, and instruments.
scoring.0: No machine-readable source identified.

evidence.label: Dataset abstract/description
evidence.value: This dataset is the June 2026 Data Release of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI; CM4AI.org), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the NIH Bridge2AI program. This Beta release includes perturb-seq data in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs and iPSC-derived NPCs, neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells in the presence of chemotherapy (vorinostat and paclitaxel); and IF images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells in the presence and absence of chemotherapy (vorinostat and paclitaxel). CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework. Data presented here will be augmented regularly through the end of the project. CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center.

criteria.practice: Provide domain-appropriate statistical characterizations of key features of the dataset to inform analysis planning. Ensure missing values are encoded consistently.

Are missing values encoded consistently?

scoring.2: Descriptive statistics of key variables are provided, and missing values are encoded consistently.
scoring.1: Missing values are encoded consistently, but no descriptive statistics are present.

evidence.value: Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturbSeq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap. Computed cell maps not included in this release.

criteria.notes: For non-tabular data this criterion is N/A. Descriptive statistics means per-variable summaries: for numeric variables, central tendency and spread with min/max and non-missing count; for categorical variables, category frequencies; plus dataset-level record and variable counts. Missing-value consistency means one documented convention used throughout (not mixed blanks/NA/-999/0).

criteria.name: Standards
criteria.practice: Provide a machine-readable data dictionary or schema for each dataset, linked to the dataset metadata, and referencing any relevant standards.
questions: Is the file governed by a formal open specification with a built-in or paired external schema that names and types its data elements? Examples include RDF/JSON-LD, OWL, OME-TIFF, OME-NGFF, NWB, WFDB, DICOM, NIfTI, Parquet, CSVW, Frictionless Table Schema, JSON Schema, XSD.

Is at least one data element bound to a standard vocabulary term through (a) a dataset-level JSON-LD sidecar, or (b) the format's inherent mechanism (vocabulary IRIs in RDF/JSON-LD data, DICOM Code Sequences, CSVW propertyUrl/aboutUrl, Frictionless rdfType, Define-XML NCI Thesaurus codes, OME annotations, NWB ontology links)?
Is the standard a true schema/model that dictates structure and content, or merely a generic file container?

scoring.2: Formal schema and at least one populated standard vocabulary binding.
scoring.1: Formal schema, no standard vocabulary binding.
scoring.0: No formal schema.

criteria.name: Potential Sources of Bias
criteria.practice: Describe known sources of bias in the data and assumptions made in collecting, processing, or interpreting the data. Include any known explanations regarding missing values, including reasons for missingness, and the degree to which data represents a state vs. a control (e.g., disease state vs. healthy state).
questions: Does the metadata describe known biases and assumptions?
Does the metadata describe, where applicable, reasons for missingness?
Does the metadata describe the state-vs-control balance?

scoring.2: Substantive description of known bias sources and assumptions in collection/processing/interpretation is given, and the applicable elements are addressed (reasons for missingness where there are missing values; state-vs-control representation where relevant).
scoring.1: Bias/assumptions are addressed but thinly, or applicable missingness/state-control elements were omitted.
scoring.0: No description of bias or assumptions is given, or a non-substantive placeholder is offered (e.g., "no known bias" with no basis).

evidence.label: Bias description (rai:dataBiases)
evidence.value: Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines, and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.

evidence.label: Missing-data reasons (rai:dataCollectionMissingData)
evidence.value: Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturbSeq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap. Computed cell maps not included in this release.

evidence.label: Completeness statement
evidence.value: These data are not yet in completed final form, and some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturbSeq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap. Computed cell maps not included in this release.

criteria.notes: "Substantive" means it engages the actual data (specific bias sources, assumptions, or reasons are named); it is not a boilerplate disclaimer. "Reasons for missingness" is N/A if the dataset has no missing values; "state-vs-control" is N/A if the dataset has no such structure. N/A elements don't count against the score.

evidence.label: Section — Use cases
evidence.value: AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics, AI/machine learning model training, cellular process analysis, cell architectural changes, and interactions in presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations. A major goal is to enable biologically-driven, interpretable ML applications, for example as proposed in Ma et al. 2018 (PMID: 29505029) and Kuenzi et al. 2020 (PMID: 33096023).

evidence.label: Section — Limitations
evidence.value: This is an interim release. It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in future releases. The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets. Requires domain expertise for meaningful analysis.

evidence.label: Section — Biases
evidence.value: Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines, and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.

evidence.label: Section — Release/maintenance plan

criteria.name: Standardized
criteria.practice: Datasets adhere to established, documented standards, including metadata standards, and their adherence can be validated deterministically.

Does a programmatic validator (e.g., script, CLI tool, or automated pipeline) exist to deterministically verify this adherence without human intervention?

scoring.2: (Meta)data conforms to a declared and documented standard (e.g., RDF/JSON-LD, OWL, OME-TIFF, OME-NGFF, NWB, WFDB, DICOM, NIfTI, Parquet, CSVW, Frictionless Table Schema, JSON Schema, XSD, GA4GH Phenopackets). Deterministic programmatic validation exists for this standard (e.g., OMOP DQD, pyshacl, JSON Schema validators), and the dataset architecture allows these tools to execute successfully.
scoring.1: (Meta)data uses a recognized file format or container (e.g., base HDF5, raw NIfTI) or conforms to a text-based specification, but it lacks a machine-readable schema. Adherence cannot be deterministically validated without manual review or custom one-off scripts.
scoring.0: No declared or documented standard is used. Data structures are arbitrary, proprietary, or undocumented, making programmatic validation impossible.

criteria.name: Computationally accessible
criteria.practice: Provide a mechanism to access data either through established exchange protocols or a well-documented API.
questions: Is there a programmatic mechanism to access the data at scale (e.g., cloud object storage, standard API)?
Does the access mechanism utilize standard interoperability protocols (e.g., GA4GH DRS, HL7 FHIR APIs, other REST API endpoints)?
Are the endpoints, payloads, and authentication methods formally documented (e.g., via an OpenAPI/Swagger specification)?

scoring.2: Programmatic access is provided via robust, formally documented APIs or standardized interoperability exchange protocols (e.g., cloud-native S3/GCS Buckets, GA4GH DRS URIs, HL7 FHIR Bulk Data Access). If the data is access-controlled, documentation explains how to gain access and the process is easily executed.
scoring.1: Programmatic access exists, but it creates friction for automated pipelines (poorly documented, non-machine-readable API documentation, custom web scraping, or non-standard authentication with human-in-the-loop steps).
scoring.0: Data is not accessible, or is accessible only via manual download, or requires direct human intervention to transfer. Also 0 if a user can access controlled-access data without permission, or a user cannot access the data despite having permission.

criteria.name: Portable

scoring.2: The data requires no specialized compute environment; OR all required resources and software dependencies are defined using standard, machine-executable deployment formats (containers, Conda environment.yml, or workflow languages such as CWL/WDL/Nextflow) so the environment can be programmatically spun up on different infrastructures.
scoring.1: Hardware constraints or software dependencies are documented in plain text (e.g., a README listing required Python versions or RAM limits), but they are not machine-executable.
scoring.0: Compute requirements and software dependencies are undocumented, or the data is tightly coupled to a proprietary system, unshareable internal cluster, or hardcoded local file paths.

criteria.name: Contextualized
criteria.practice: Include any considerations regarding splits of the data, including any information withheld at any point of data collection and processing. Provide examples of data components to aid understanding of their general structure and content.

Is any withheld information (such as de-identified/redacted fields, censored variables, or blinded evaluation holdouts) clearly described?
Are representative examples or synthetic datasets provided that strictly mirror the structure of the full dataset?

scoring.2: The dataset composition is transparent. Any predefined splits are explicitly defined (including stratification strategies or random seeds), OR the dataset is explicitly documented as not requiring splits. Redacted, censored, or blinded data is clearly detailed. Crucially, machine-readable example data (a synthetic set or representative subset) is provided.
scoring.1: Context is provided but incomplete (splits mentioned without methodology; withheld data noted vaguely; or examples provided in a non-actionable format such as a PDF screenshot).
scoring.0: No context is provided regarding splits, withheld information, or structural examples.
